title: London weather today hour by hour as temperatures hit 1C | London Now
text:
Londoners face a bitterly cold morning as temperatures fall to just 1C (Image: Danny Lawson/PA) 

 Londoners face a bitterly cold start to today, with temperatures expected to plunge to just 1C during the morning commute. 

 After a chilly day yesterday, the capital is set for another cold spell, despite the clear skies and sunshine predicted for much of the day. 

 Forecasts suggest temperatures will peak at around 8C in the afternoon, before sharply dropping again overnight. 

 Chillier temperatures are expected around 7am, making for an especially brisk morning commute. 

 However, despite the freezing conditions, Londoners can anticipate a largely dry day, with significant sunshine and almost no chance of rain. 

 The forecast indicates just a one per cent chance of precipitation during the day, resulting in a bright but cold end to the working week. 

## Hour-by-hour forecast 

 Here's what the weather is expected to be like, hour by hour, today: 

 6am: 2C - A cold start to the morning, with clear skies and dry conditions. 

 7am: 1C - Temperatures reach their lowest point, making for a particularly chilly commute. 

 8am: 2C - Sunshine starts to appear, though temperatures stay close to freezing. 

 9am: 2C - Clear and sunny skies continue as temperatures gradually rise. 

 10am: 4C - London enjoys a bright morning, with sunshine and little chance of rain. 

 11am: 5C - Temperatures continue to increase, although conditions remain chilly. 

 12pm: 7C - A sunny lunchtime is expected, with temperatures reaching about 7C. 

 1pm: 8C - The warmest part of the day, with clear skies and plenty of sunshine. 

 2pm: 8C - Sunshine continues across the capital, with temperatures staying around 8C. 

 3pm: 7C - A bright but increasingly chilly afternoon as daylight begins to fade. 

 4pm: 7C - Sunny conditions continue before sunset, with temperatures starting to fall. 

 5pm: 6C - Clear skies are expected as the city heads into the evening. 

 6pm: 5C - Temperatures continue to drop, with dry and clear conditions. 

 7pm: 4C - A cold evening is forecast, with little cloud and no significant rainfall expected. 

 8pm: 4C - Clear skies continue, with temperatures remaining in low single figures. 

 9pm: 3C - Temperatures fall further as London heads towards another cold night. 

 10pm: 3C - Mostly clear conditions are expected, with temperatures remaining around 3C. 

 11pm: 3C - The day ends with mostly clear skies and chilly conditions. 

## Will it rain? 

 London is set to remain rain-free throughout today, with just a one per cent chance of precipitation. 

 Clear skies and sunshine are forecast for much of the day, providing a break from the wetter and cloudier weather earlier this week. 

 However, the absence of cloud cover overnight will also allow temperatures to drop, posing a frost risk in some areas. 

## Could there be frost? 

 With temperatures expected to dip to around 1C in the morning, frost is a possibility in parts of the capital. 

 Outer London boroughs such as Bexley, Bromley, Croydon, and Sutton may experience colder conditions than central London, particularly in more open or rural areas. 

 However, temperatures will vary locally, and frost is not guaranteed everywhere. 

 Drivers heading out early may want to allow extra time to clear frost from their windscreens. 

 Those walking or cycling should also be cautious, as exposed surfaces could become slippery where moisture has frozen. 

## How cold will it get tonight? 

 Temperatures are set to drop again after sunset, with readings falling to around 3C by late evening. 

 The wider forecast suggests temperatures could dip to approximately 0C overnight, potentially resulting in another frosty start to Saturday. 

 With clear skies expected, the cold conditions could be particularly noticeable for Londoners planning to head out on Friday evening.

title: London weather expert gives snow verdict and predicts when temperatures will dip to freezing - My London
text:
Temperatures could plummet to freezing in London as soon as the latter half of this week, according to a weather expert. London’s peripheral zones - including areas like Croydon - could drop to 0C on Friday (November 13) and Saturday (November 14), according to Jim Dale of the British Weather Services.

This could make for a miserable end of the week, especially following on from the fog warning earlier today (Tuesday, November 10). Jim also explained why it's the outer areas of the city that would feel a dip in temperatures more starkly than areas deeper into London.

It’s because London is an ‘urban heat island, heat radiates away, and rural surfaces tend to radiate it away faster.’ In short, the further in to the centre you go, the less likely it is to feel quite as cold. It would still be cold, of course, just not quite as cold as the areas where the buildings are spaced further apart.

He did rule out snow this month, though, and said that although December, a winter month, is where you would see snow, we may well not due to 'El Nino and climate change.'

...

It won’t exactly be nice for the rest of this week. Tonight will remain cloudy and wet, with spells of rain lingering throughout the night, these heavy in places.

Tomorrow (Wednesday, November 10) will continue largely cloudy, and early rain will soon clear away.

It will then be dry in the afternoon, and a few brighter breaks are possible towards the north in spots.
